newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's buys 80 pct of drinks firm stock.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's buys 80 pct of drinks firm stock.

text.p: Morocco's largest beverage bottling and brewery Brasseries du Maroc purchased 80 percent of soft drinks firm Societe Indusrielle Marocaine (SIM) for $52 million, a senior company official said on Thursday.

"We purchased 80 percent of SIM company at $52 million with 50 percent of this amount provided by Coca Cola Middle East company," M'Fadel Lahlou, chairman of Brasseries du Maroc board of directors told Reuters.
Lahlou is also head of Societe Nationale d'Investissement, one of Brasseries du Maroc's main shareholders.
"After we signed the purchase agreement with SIM, we signed another accord with Coca Cola for a $26 million medium term loan," Lahlou said.
The loan allowed for the purchase of SIM "which is of strategic and financial importance for us...It will help us expand our business in Morocco," Lahlou said.
Brasseries du Maroc controls 95 percent of Morocco's beer market. It also manufactures under licence Coca Cola and Heineken brands.
"Our move aimed to enhance distribution of Coca Cola products to meet the domestic increasing demand for soft drinks," the firm's leader said.
Brasseries du Maroc will benefit from SIM's logistics of 280 distribution's vehicles and more than 50,000 clients, Lahlou added.
An analyst at Upline Securities said Brasseries du Maroc, which has an annual bottling capacity of 2.3 million hectolitres, started a three-year strategic plan in January.

"Brasseries du Maroc net income should have recorded 15 percent increase to 160 million dirhams in 1996. Another 7.0 percent growth is expected in 1997. However, this last forecast will be largely higher as the market rumours of the firm's takeover of SIM were confirmed on Thursday," Upline Securities said.
Upline said Brasseries du Maroc has a number of outstanding shares of 2.8 million and a market capitalisation of 5.2 billion dirhams.
One of the 47 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, Brasseries du Maroc was last traded at 1,870 dirhams.
